clue.text: Swapped men seeing players were in front

parts.note: the players in a show are its cast
led means were in front, past tense of lead

explanation.surface: A team changes its line-up after seeing the opposition take the lead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swapped men' is a chess move: the king and a rook trade places in one turn.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess, the move that moves king and rook together in one turn is named after the rook, the castle piece.

clue.text: Cold cold hearts, sick facing empty end

indicators.note: facing puts the earlier pieces up against the final one

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
H is the card abbreviation for hearts
ill means sick

indicators.note: empty means take out the inside letters, keeping only the outsides of end

explanation.surface: Someone with a cold heart is sickened as they face a bleak end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'empty' reduces 'end' to its outer letters, ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something cooled right down is cold, so the adjectives are synonyms.

clue.text: Study reportedly brought down corporation

indicators.note: reportedly means as it is said, so the word for brought down is only heard

parts.note: sank means brought down, as with a ship
corporation is an old jokey word for a pot belly, a tum

explanation.surface: A report about a company brought down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' makes SANK sound like SANC. Corporation for a paunch is old British humour.
explanation.definitionFit: A study can be a private room where one works undisturbed, an inner retreat.

clue.text: Old railway company possesses single means of transport

indicators.note: possesses means holds, so the railway letters hold the single letter

parts.note: the LNER was the London and North Eastern Railway, a British company from 1923 to 1947
single means one, the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A historic railway firm owns just one way of getting about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possesses' puts I inside LNER.
explanation.definitionFit: An ocean-going passenger ship carries people over the sea, a kind of transport.

clue.text: Lays bare round ends overlapping

indicators.note: overlapping means the two words share a letter where they meet, so one copy goes

parts.note: a disc is a round flat object
closes means ends or finishes

explanation.surface: Someone strips off around the edges, the ends overlapping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overlapping' means DISC and CLOSES share their C, written once.
explanation.definitionFit: To reveal or expose a secret is to uncover it, laying it open.

clue.text: Etiquette of French? Well, I'm not sure

parts.note: de is French for of
cor is an exclamation of surprise, like well!
um is the noise of hesitation

explanation.surface: Someone asked about French manners hesitates over the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean proper behaviour and polite conduct by the accepted rules.

clue.text: Gorgeous girl not forthcoming

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana
shy means reserved, not forthcoming

explanation.surface: A beautiful girl who keeps herself to herself.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishy is informal British for good-looking or attractive.

clue.text: High point of teaching taking short view

indicators.note: taking means taking in, so the teaching word holds the shortened view

parts.note: a credo is a creed or doctrine, a teaching

indicators.note: short means the last letter of the word for view is cut off

parts.note: a scene is a view

explanation.surface: A teacher's best moment comes from adopting a narrow outlook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' drops the final E of the view word; 'taking' sets what is left inside the teaching word.
explanation.definitionFit: Strictly a gradual rise in volume, it is widely used for the peak or climax that rise reaches.

clue.text: May's core politician in raving frenzy

indicators.note: the politician's letters sit inside the raving word

parts.note: raving means wild fury, a rage

indicators.note: the core of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: Theresa May's inner circle of politicians go into a wild fury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'core' takes A, the middle letter of 'May's'; 'in' sets it and the politician inside the fury word. Theresa May was a British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: A wild bout of violent, uncontrolled behaviour is a frenzy.

clue.text: Old bedsit oddly covered by fancy simplicity

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside the exclamation's letters

parts.note: fancy! and my! are both exclamations of surprise

indicators.note: oddly means take the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the words Old bedsit

explanation.surface: A shabby old bedsit is dressed up in finery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' takes O, D, E, S, T from 'Old bedsit', and 'covered by' puts them inside MY.
explanation.definitionFit: Lack of show or pretension, plainness and unassuming manner, is a sense of simplicity.

clue.text: Period when bats fly around?

parts.note: bats are cricket batsmen, and this is the spell when they are at the crease swinging away, not flying mammals at dusk

explanation.surface: A question about the hour when bats come out and flit about.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batsmen are often called bats; their turn at batting has its own name.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, a player's or team's turn at batting is this word, the spell when the batters are in action.

clue.text: Journalist following second eleven moved quickly

indicators.note: the journalist's letters come after the other pieces, so following places them last

parts.note: a cricket or football side has eleven players, a team
ed is short for editor

explanation.surface: A reporter tails the reserve side as it hurries along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eleven' looks like part of 'second eleven', a reserve team, but the words split: second gives S and eleven a team.
explanation.definitionFit: To go at full steam is to rush, so the past tense describes hurrying along.

clue.text: American measure facing supporter closely

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece facing another sits in front of it

parts.note: liter is the American spelling of the metric unit of volume
an ally is someone who backs you

explanation.surface: A US unit of volume is set right beside its backer.
explanation.walkthrough: The American spelling matters: the British spelling would put the E and R the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: A translation done word for word follows the text exactly, sticking tightly to the original.

clue.text: Men in confusion bottling up pressure for nothing

indicators.note: the word for confusion holds the new letter inside it, so bottling up shows where it goes
pressure for nothing means the pressure letter takes the place of the nothing letter

parts.note: chaos is utter confusion
O, the zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: Men in turmoil keep their stress bottled up rather than let it out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottling up' and 'for' put P in place of the O in CHAOS.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaps is informal British talk for men or fellows.

clue.text: Checks edge of smashed guitar gear?

indicators.note: the edge of a word here is its final letter

parts.note: electric guitars are played through amps, short for amplifiers

explanation.surface: A rock fan asks whether the amplifiers were wrecked along with the guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edge of' takes the last letter of 'smashed', D.
explanation.definitionFit: To dampen or restrain, as in damping enthusiasm, is to curb or hold back.

clue.text: Representative, American, promoted bishop before old 'scandal'

indicators.note: before places the earlier pieces ahead of the old scandal
promoted means moved up, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: US means American
RR, Right Reverend, is the title of a bishop
-gate is the suffix for a scandal, after Watergate

explanation.surface: An American delegate rises above a bishop's old scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promoted' reads US upwards as SU.
explanation.definitionFit: A substitute or stand-in acting for someone is their representative.

clue.text: Extraordinarily dirty place hiding robber's first treasure

indicators.note: the dirty place wraps round the other letters, hiding them inside

parts.note: a sty, a pigsty, is a filthy place

indicators.note: first takes the opening letter of the word robber's

parts.note: a lovely person is called a treasure or an angel

explanation.surface: A thief has stashed his loot in some filthy den.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' takes R from 'robber's', and 'hiding' sets it and the treasure word inside the pigsty.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean in an unusual or peculiar way, so the adverbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Right about flipping naked desperate man being unemployed

indicators.note: about means around, so the right letters go round the rest
flipping means turning over, so the word for naked is read backwards

parts.note: nude means naked
Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British comic The Dandy

explanation.surface: A desperate naked man flips out over losing his job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' gives EDUN; 'about' wraps the right letters round it and the comic hero. Desperate Dan is the strongman of the British comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker made surplus to needs and laid off is out of work.

clue.text: Stunned senior forced to take on United

indicators.note: to take on means to admit or bring in, so the united letter is taken in

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
prised means levered or forced open

explanation.surface: An elderly man made to sign for Manchester United is left dumbfounded.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to take on' slots the United letter in just after the first letter of the senior abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken aback by the unexpected leaves one amazed, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Gets undressed turning back to hide one's feelings

indicators.note: to hide means to hold inside, so the reversed word holds the one
turning back means the word for gets undressed is read in reverse

parts.note: strips means takes off clothes
one is I, the Roman numeral; one's here is one is

explanation.surface: Someone undresses, then turns away to hide their emotions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' makes STRIPS into SPIRTS, and 'to hide' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mood or state of mind, as in high or low spirits, means one's feelings.

clue.text: Sailor put up on chains missing right tack

indicators.note: in a down clue on means placed above, so the sailor comes first
put up means raised, so in a down clue the letters read upwards

parts.note: tar is a sailor

indicators.note: missing means without, so a letter is dropped from the chains

parts.note: irons are chains or fetters

explanation.surface: A sailor clapped in chains, without any right to change tack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put up' turns TAR into RAT; 'missing' drops R from IRONS to leave IONS. Tack is old slang for food, as in hardtack.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is an old word for food, as in hardtack, and allotted portions of food are rations.

clue.text: One's performance entails ruddy aria initially

definitions.text: One's performance entails ruddy aria initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the five words before it

explanation.surface: A singer's turn comes with a confounded aria.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and a description: a stage work whose performance includes arias.
explanation.definitionFit: A staged musical drama typically features sung solos, so a show that includes an aria fits.

clue.text: Manuscript absorbing Queen penned by period author

indicators.note: penned by means shut in by, so the period encloses the rest

parts.note: an eon is a vast period of time

indicators.note: absorbing means taking in, so the manuscript letters hold the queen

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: A royal manuscript written by a writer of the era.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' and 'penned by' nest the Queen inside the manuscript inside the period. Ralph Waldo Emerson was an American essayist.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Waldo Emerson was a nineteenth-century American essayist and poet, so a writer.

clue.text: Excerpt of part is testing performer

indicators.note: Excerpt of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A bit of the role is proving hard to play.
explanation.definitionFit: An entertainer such as a singer or dancer is a professional performer.

clue.text: Captivated by paint, Rothko's beginning

indicators.note: captivated by means held captive inside the words that follow, so the letters are taken from within them

explanation.surface: A viewer is enthralled by the paint of Mark Rothko's early work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Captivated by' takes the letters from inside 'paint, Rothko's'. Mark Rothko was an American abstract painter.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is a short form of introduction, the opening section of a piece.

clue.text: Feeling thrilled, the setter proposed, losing heart

parts.note: sent is slang for thrilled or carried away
the setter refers to themself as I

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letter of the word for proposed is dropped

parts.note: meant means intended or proposed

explanation.surface: The compiler, carried away, proposes but loses courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' drops A, the middle letter, from MEANT, leaving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe an emotion or attitude someone holds.

clue.text: Prison supports last of uniforms with time done

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so prison goes below
last of means take the final letter of the word uniforms

parts.note: a pen is an enclosure, slang for a prison

explanation.surface: A convict in uniform finishes their sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last of' takes S, the final letter of 'uniforms'.
explanation.definitionFit: When energy or money is used up it is finished, all gone.

clue.text: State of India shook unevenly

indicators.note: unevenly means take the odd-placed letters, first, third, fifth, of the words India shook

explanation.surface: A region of India suffered an irregular tremor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unevenly' takes the 1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th and 9th letters of 'India shook'.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is one of the fifty United States, in the Pacific Northwest.

clue.text: Ego run down comprehending love produces divorce

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

indicators.note: comprehending means taking in or including, so the critic's word holds the love letter

parts.note: to slate is to criticise or run down
love is zero in tennis, O

explanation.surface: A self-absorbed partner who keeps putting the other down brings about a split.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehending' puts O inside SLATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To divorce something is to separate it or cut it off from the rest, used as a verb.

clue.text: Service in main reflecting collects

indicators.note: the service sits inside the reflected sea
reflecting means mirrored, so the word for main is read backwards

parts.note: the main is old poetic language for the open sea
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: A church service held at sea is mirrored in the water and gathers people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflecting' gives AES from the sea word, and 'in' sets the service inside it. The main is the open sea.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather in quantity or accumulate is to pile up, the same as gathering together.

clue.text: Dubious party wielding useless power

indicators.note: wielding means holding in the hand, so the faction holds the other letters

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
u/s, short for unserviceable, means useless

explanation.surface: A shady political faction holding power it cannot use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wielding' wraps the party round the other letters; useless as u/s, unserviceable, is military jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adjective it means open to doubt or questionable.

clue.text: Best coat for tiger cat

indicators.note: a coat is an outer layer, so the coat for a word is its outside letters

parts.note: the ounce is another name for the snow leopard

explanation.surface: Picking the finest coat for a big cat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat for' takes the outer letters of 'tiger', TR.
explanation.definitionFit: To best someone is to beat them, and the answer means defeat thoroughly.
